rounds.text: Venmax Drugs & Pharmaceuticals Ltd presents a concerning financial profile characterized by severe cash flow instability and deteriorating ownership confidence. The company reported a negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -11.00 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a deeply problematic cash conversion ratio of -44.00x [E28, E29, E30]. This lack of liquidity is compounded by a significant decline in promoter interest, with holdings dropping from 23.13% to 10.46% over the last three years [E34, E49]. Valuation metrics appear disconnected from underlying performance, as the stock trades at a P/E of 46.6x, which is notably higher than the sector benchmark of 31.02x [E1, E6]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability remains weak, evidenced by a return on capital employed of only 2.48% compared to the sector benchmark of 11.56% [E10]. The stock’s poor momentum is reflected in its -58% one-year share price growth and its position at only 5% of its 52-week range [E5, E22]. Conceded: the company has successfully reduced its debt to 0.00x and demonstrated strong compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16, E31, E32].
